correctness.rationale: The normalized harmonic completion maps D conformally into the vertical strip, hence ω=Φ^{-1}F is a disk self-map with ω(0)=0. Schwarz gives holomorphic quotient g=ω/z bounded by one and q=max_{|z|≤r}|g|. For q>0, ψ(z)=ω(rz)/(qr) maps the unit disk into itself fixing zero, and Littlewood subordination of the subharmonic |U(qrz)|^p yields the claimed norm inequality; q=0 gives zero. Since Φ′=4/(π(1+z²)) never vanishes, Δ|U|^p>0 on open portions of every annulus off U=0 for p>1, so circular means M_p strictly increase for radius>0. Thus equality forces q=1; g achieves interior modulus one and is a unimodular constant, making f exactly a rotation of sign(cos θ). Conversely rotations attain sharp norm by source Proposition 2.1. The q=0 and p>1 endpoints are handled.
residual_risks: The theorem excludes p=1, r=0, complex boundary data, and a true boundary-space stability estimate.
